testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Manual air tank drains should be:

options.text: Opened to drain the tanks every day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opened to drain the tanks every day.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in a brake system collects water and oil. These can damage the brakes. You must open manual air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When stopping in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop.
Veer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight. You may need to turn, so stay in control while braking.

questions.question: Brakes out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes that are out of adjustment wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums before each trip. It is unsafe to drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on, you should:

options.text: Continue driving and have brakes repaired within a week.
Pull over and inspect the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and inspect the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop your vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes. Inspect and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: The air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold enough air for one brake use only.
Hold enough air to brake several times if the compressor stops working.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air to brake several times if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air to use the brakes several times even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are inside the drum brake.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air. It stops pumping if tank pressure gets too high and starts pumping if pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) gives you better control during hard braking. It does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Air brakes use compressed air to operate. Many large trucks have air brake systems.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These substances can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you should:

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, pull each slack adjuster to check it. It should not move more than about one inch. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: What is often found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because water collects in the tanks from compressed air
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because water collects in the tanks from compressed air
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil that build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain tanks at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure gets too low, the springs activate the brakes.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the first reservoir. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators are:

options.text: Used to add alcohol to braking systems to prevent freezing.
Only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used to add alcohol to braking systems to prevent freezing.
questions.explanation: Alcohol evaporators add alcohol to the braking system to prevent ice from forming, which can damage the system.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal activates while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop where you are and park
Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning activates, safely exit the roadway and park as soon as possible. Low air pressure means the brakes may not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It does not work with air brakes.
It does not help in most driving situations.
It helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air brakes and helps drivers stay in control by stopping wheels from locking up.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into your view when air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: What does an S-cam do when it turns inside a brake drum?

options.text: It presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
It presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
It presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the pedal
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the pedal
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through the brake lines. There is a delay of at least half a second between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work.

questions.question: What shows you the air pressure in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.
